steps.text: Muffled thunder rumbles behind dark clouds, startling Vetochki awake from her dream.
If one can even call a mess of frightening scenes quickly shifting from one to another a 'dream' at all. Fortunately, it has just ended.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: ...I, fell asleep? For, how long?
The leader of the ad-hoc rescue squad remains fixated on her own dagger, and just as Vetochki thinks her question will not be answered, the dagger is quickly sheathed.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: 'Asleep'?
The squad leader grabs Vetochki's hand, who now realizes her own stiff fingers are still balled into a fist, nails embedded into her palm.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: You fainted on the battlefield.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: I'm sorry...

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: Give me the box.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: W-what?

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: Me-di-cine. Box. Give it to me.
Before Departure
Londinium, Rhodes Island branch office

steps.name: Medical Department Operator
steps.text: One second, I'll sign it once I'm done with this medicine list.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Th-Thank you!

steps.name: Medical Department Operator
steps.text: Have you gotten the mission briefing yet? Seems like a no. Here, I'll print you a copy. Let's see... Child refugees from a shelter outside the city have gone missing?

steps.name: Medical Department Operator
steps.text: I remember the place, on the border to the barrens. A kind old man established that shelter. After the war, many homeless Infected children began to call the shelter their home.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: I heard... they, ran off, on their own...
Vetochki bites her tongue, holding back from saying anything further.

steps.name: Medical Department Operator
steps.text: Well, it is close to the barrens after all. It's impossible to compare it to Londinium or any other nomadic city.

steps.name: Medical Department Operator
steps.text: Food shortages, wild beast attacks, active Originium... Even with people to protect the place, it's a hard life out there.

steps.name: Medical Department Operator
steps.text: ...You get what I mean, Vetochki?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Medical Department Operator
steps.text: Sigh. If I were your primary doctor, I'd never allow you to take on such a dangerous mission before your condition's stable.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: I, I saw photos... of those kids. I want, to help them.

steps.name: Medical Department Operator
steps.text: 'Help' is a good reason—but it's not enough. Take these pills. I trust you know how to use them?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Y-Yes.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: (Knocks on door)

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: What's taking so long? Isn't it just a letter of consent?

steps.name: Medical Department Operator
steps.text: Tch... Don't be so scared by your leader, Vetochki. Her fierce front's just a facade.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Doctor... Leader, you two know, each other?

steps.name: Medical Department Operator
steps.text: Could say she's a friend of mine. I already had her promise me she'd take care of you on the road—By that I mean, make sure you take your medicine regularly.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: Ti—ck, to—ck, tick tock!

steps.name: Medical Department Operator
steps.text: Listen now, Vetochki. I don't care how you convinced HR to let you join this field operation...

steps.name: Medical Department Operator
steps.text: But as a doctor, I have one piece of advice; and as a friend, a similar request—

steps.name: Medical Department Operator
steps.text: Take your medicine on time, and don't put your own life in danger. Got it, Vetochki?
The Medical Department Operator signs the consent letter, and solemnly places it into Vetochki's hands.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: Time to move out. Make sure you keep your pills safely stored.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: So, where's the medicine box?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: ...I, have it. Here.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: You haven't taken even one pill?

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: Why?
Vetochki squeezes her lips tightly and does not answer.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: ...Tell me again, our mission objective.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Go to... the wasteland, and find the, missing Infected, children.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Then, bring them back, to the city, for treatment.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: You chose to join us on this mission. Tell me why.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Because, I want to, help them. I want to help, more Infected...

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: Now tell me why I agreed to let you come with me then.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: I, promised you... I won't... cause trouble.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: And did you manage that?

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: You fainted in battle. We couldn't just leave you there, we had to stop.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: Those kids will have to wait half a day more.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: I'm... sorry...

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: No. Now's not the time for apologies.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: Just wanted you to know everything happens for a reason. I let you on this mission because I can see you were once like those kids—all of us were. That's why I said yes.
The squad leader points at the medicine box.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: Now I want to know your reason.
Vetochki shies away from her leader's gaze. The next second, a surface wound stings her with pain, spreading into her insides.
She cannot help curling up, but stops herself from making any sound.
Large beads of cold sweat roll down her head, and Vetochki knows the inflammation caused by Oripathy is damaging her nerves. She is all too familiar with this kind of pain.
Her leader hurriedly opens the medicine box, and pours out a bunch of individually packed painkiller tablets. She peels one open, and stuffs it into Vetochki's mouth.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: The pain will stop soon.
Vetochki swallows the pill. Rhodes Island's specially created painkillers for acute inflammations work well, and usually take effect within five to ten minutes.
The pill's composition includes algae extracts as a sweetener. But the refreshing taste sends Vetochki into tears.
She cannot verbalize why she is crying. After all... the pain will stop soon.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: I heard my friend mention that you were always cooperative with your treatments. So... why haven't you been taking your painkillers?
Vetochki also looks toward the pile of pills. It is obvious that the amount is far more than the dosage allocated to her by the doctor for this mission.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Before I, came to Rhodes Island... I never, heard of this—'painkiller'.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: We also, had in the mines, a kind of, medicine. But they... were super bitter, and made your head dizzy. But the pain, would go away.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: I've heard of the situation in Ursus. That Emperor did try a little, yet could not ensure his little shred of benevolence would make it down to the bottom rungs of society.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: Rhodes Island's medicine is naturally better than what you could get outside, but does it not suit you?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: They're... too sweet...

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: No, I, I don't know...

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: When I tried, a real painkiller on Rhodes Island, for the first time, I realized...
Vetochki takes a deep breath to manage an uninterrupted sentence.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: ...I couldn't feel anything at all.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: I don't, like pain... but for so, many years, it's my most, familiar feeling.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: Treating pain itself as something you can't live without... I don't see it as necessary at all, but of course, you may think I have no right to say that.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: I can give you ten more minutes of rest, but after that the squad will move. You can come with us, or you can go back for treatment.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: L-leader!
Vetochki picks up the scattered pills, and tries to stabilize her voice for a question—

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: But, if the pain, we feel, has always been, part of us...

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Doesn't that mean, it's there for, a reason?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: I don't, fully understand, but I'm scared... to lose it.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: ...If you choose to come with us, then you'll have to take your medicine on time. There won't be a second warning from me.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Archer
steps.text: (Quietly) Stay alert.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: Did you hear something?

steps.name: Rescue Squad Archer
steps.text: Wild tuskbeasts barking... more than one of them around. In a specific rhythm too—they're surrounding their prey and trying to intimidate it.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: P-Prey?

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: Just an act of intimidation, but that means they're not attacking yet. Can you make out any sounds from the children?

steps.name: Rescue Squad Archer
steps.text: (Shakes head)

steps.name: Rescue Squad Archer
steps.text: Tuskbeasts are fierce in packs, and we have ways to disperse them, but I'm worried their barks might attract the bigger guys.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Big... like manglerbeasts? We should...

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: Point us the way, and we'll hurry. Vetochki, you follow at the very back.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: But I... I!

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: We can't rule out this being a trap just yet. Remember our route, and if we need to retreat, you'll become the lead.
The squad leader stops talking, and takes her dagger from her waist, placing it into Vetochki's hands, then immediately runs forward.
A torch lights up, waved by a girl insistent on driving the ravenous beasts away.

steps.name: Injured Girl
steps.text: Get lost!
The beasts are patient, staring at the beads of blood tumbling down nonstop, waiting for time to help them put the fire out.

steps.name: Injured Girl
steps.text: Don't, cry... no crying!

steps.name: Injured Girl
steps.text: Crying will only attract more beasts!
The girl throws a handful of sand to stop the children trying to come closer to help her.
She cannot tell if she regrets bringing the children along on her escape from the shelter.

steps.name: Injured Girl
steps.text: Wait until they kill me... then you guys keep on running. Londinium has Oripathy medicine... reach the city and you'll survive!
The torch's light suddenly shrinks, and the wild beasts pounce from the darkness, baring their sharp claws and fangs at her—
Hold it!
Multiple figures burst forth from the shadows. A shield lands with a solid thud in front of her.
The girl thinks about how to respond when a tuskbeast knocked onto the ground earlier jumps right back up from her side and bites her neck.
No!!

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: D-Don't be scared...

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: We already, chased them off. You are, all safe now.
The collapsed bell tower is riddled with scars of battle. From broken floorboards and scorched rock, multiple pairs of eyes peer out in her direction.
The stench of blood pervades the air, and for a moment, everyone is speechless, unsure what they should say to the children.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: They should be the children we're looking for. A group of mostly Sarkaz, infected by Oripathy during the war.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: Vetochki, do another headcount.

steps.name: Infected Child
steps.text: S-Stay back!

steps.name: Infected Child
steps.text: My sister...

steps.name: Infected Child
steps.text: Is she dead?
Vetochki stops in her tracks. The child talks of death with such a calm voice—she finds the feeling familiar, yet frightening.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: No, she's not.
The girl fighting off the pack alone earlier is lifted by the rescue squad's other members onto a flat surface.
Then, they set up emergency lights and operation equipment.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: Prepare for trachea incision.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: Vetochki, hand me my dagger.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Dag...ger?

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: Yes. My dagger.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: Preparing for intubation. Someone take over.

steps.name: Injured Girl
steps.text: Hrrh... Hrrh...
Under the light, Vetochki finally gets a good look at the girl and the other children hidden beneath the bell tower's ruins.
They are quite young, yet there are scary black stones all over their bodies.
Festering wounds, blood seeping through cloth, blank faces hollowed from the pain... Vetochki is momentarily stunned by the sight.
These children hiding in the ruins immediately walk over to Vetochki, looking at the girl with blood all over her with complicated emotions.

steps.name: Infected Child
steps.text: Did she make it?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: I don't know...

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: She's conscious again, even if barely. Yes, she's alive.
Vetochki looks at the squad leader, who shakes her head ever so slightly.
A few of the children sit down as if a burden has finally lifted off their shoulders, and now their tears and fears flow freely.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: We come from Rhodes Island, on a mission from a Mr. White of Woodland Shelter to save you. We'll escort you out of the wastes.

steps.name: Infected Child
steps.text: No. We don't want to go back!

steps.name: Infected Child
steps.text: Tell Mr. White we're sorry—but we wanna live!

steps.name: Infected Child
steps.text: Our sister said, only Londinium has the medicine that can heal us!

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: But you don't even know where it is. Londinium is behind you, actually. If we didn't make it to you guys on time, you would've all died out here in the wild.

steps.name: Infected Child
steps.text: We want to go to Londinium! It's what our sister told us!

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: You have to, get your, wounds treated...
Watching these crying and injured children, Vetochki suddenly realizes something, and hurries to open her bag, dumping the contents onto the ground.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: What are you—

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Medicine! They—help them!
Vetochki grabs her secret stash of painkillers, and places them one by one into each child's hand.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Eat it. Pain will stop soon.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: I have many! So you won't, feel any more pain!
Her face reddens as she tries to calm her throat so she can tell the kids how they should take the medicine, but—
Vetochki takes a deep breath instead, removes the packaging from a pill, and eats it as the children watch.
And so they follow, swallowing their medicine.
She nods, then turns around, planning to hand the leftover pills to the girl they were calling 'sister' earlier.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: It won't work on her.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: But she's... awake...

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: Vetochki!

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: (Whispering) There is no medicine that can stop her particular kind of pain—that's death. The painkiller she needs now is not the pills you have.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: (Whispering) Let her watch these children for as long as she can.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: (Whispering) She was the one who brought them out into the wastes, yet she was also their guardian.
No one else speaks, and tears no longer fall. Only harsh huffs can be heard in the ruins, like the sound of a ruptured bellows—the anguished hollow howls from the dying.
Vetochki rubs the pills in her hand, numbly watching the girl refusing to die. For just a brief moment, their gazes seem to meet.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: It's time to take the kids away.

steps.name: Infected Child
steps.text: Where are you taking us, sister?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: 'Sister'?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: We... are going to Londinium.
Vetochki has no idea if the city will be kind to these Sarkaz children, but she makes a vow to herself—
She will keep them safe on this journey, until they reach the 'Londinium' that can treat their sickness.

steps.name: Infected Child
steps.text: Thank you for the candy, sister. The pain really stopped.
Vetochki stops in her tracks when she suddenly realizes the raspy gasps from the bell tower have already ceased at some point.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: Vetochki.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: I just, took the medicine... the box is here, look.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: Hm. I see. Very good.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: I have something to show you too.
The squad leader opens her collar button, exposing a shocking depression on her neck, where a web of scars seems to spread all the way to her jaw.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: What is... this?

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: It's complicated, but basically, shrapnel cut a bit of bone off with some flesh too.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: That was, painful, right?

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: Yes. I only knew later that the bone was linked to multiple nerves connected to the brain. Even after I left the battlefield for the hospital bed, I would still feel excruciating pain.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: I would even scratch the wound that was only beginning to heal in the hopes of relieving my suffering, only to make it bleed non-stop. It'd turn half my pillow red in just two hours.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: I got scolded many times, by that very same doctor who signed your form. Then we became friends.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: So, what do you, mean?

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: I didn't answer your question back then, because some answers aren't enough with just talk. You have to look, think, and come to the realization yourself.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: What 'pain' means to me, in life... I still, don't know.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: You do. You just don't have the means to put it into words.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: I found my answer during my sleepless nights on my sickbed. But only after a decade or so, I finally managed to form my feelings into a sentence.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: So what, is it?

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: The pain you feel makes you want to change, to live on.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Ah...

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: Not so much of a surprise, is it? I said before, you should've known long ago.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: That's not, what I'm sad about...

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Back then, when I was, in Ursus...

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Over there, even if I, wanted to end my, own life, it was not, allowed.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: All of us, had no power, to make any change.
Vetochki recalls her comrades on the tundra, the long, long line of miners she used to count over and over.
Each time she reached the end of the line, the number she bit back was a little smaller than the last.
'...Seven hundred and twenty-three.'
'...Seven hundred and twenty-two.'
'...Seven hundred and twenty-one.'
She knows a life stands behind every number—surviving was good enough, but she also knew when they set off, the headcounts used to start with a 'Nine.'

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: But at least you can change, right now. Change yourself, or perhaps others.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: 'Change'?
Vetochki recalls the children's faces at the bell tower, remembers how they ate the 'candy' she gave them.
Have those faces changed? Did she... change anything? Was it her, or the pills that did it?
She repeatedly chews on the word in her mind to mine the meaning within.
Her squad leader pats her on the shoulder, then gets up and prepares to leave.
But Vetochki stops her.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Leader, your dagger...
Vetochki remembers returning the dagger to her leader after that emergency surgical operation, but now, it is nowhere to be found on her leader's waist.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: (Whispering) There is no medicine that can stop her particular kind of pain—that's death...

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: The painkiller she needs now is not the pills you have.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: It's time to take the kids away.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: I gave my dagger to her.

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: She didn't want to die in front of all those kids she brought out from the shelter, and she shouldn't have to suffer a prolonged, painful punishment for her act of bravery...

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: Before you even ask 'How did you know', if I fall one day in a place like that, when you see the only expression I can muster, you'll understand.
The squad leader walks outside the tent once she is done speaking.
The other members have already made sure the children are also ready to go anytime.
An order is declared, and the group is quick to assemble and march back towards Londinium.
They have spent too much time here with the sun about to rise, but Vetochki is not sure of her directions. She does not know where the sun will rise.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Will we... return?

steps.name: Rescue Squad Leader
steps.text: Once they're escorted into a safe area, I'll go back to fetch the girl.
Vetochki stares at her leader's empty dagger sheath for a long time as the ruined bell tower builds itself back in all sorts of ways in her head.
The sun creeps up from the horizon, and the dim rays cast a long shadow of the tower ruins onto the ground.
Vetochki puts down her shield in that direction, and raises a fist—
Thump.
Again and again, she hits her own shield, like striking a bell.
The metal ringing startles many creatures out on the wastes from their slumber.
She endures the pain, staring right at the sun as it gradually turns whole, walking towards the splendor until tears obscure her vision entirely.
